description:
The four presentation decks under `docs/presentations/` belong to archived epics. They move, with their complete asset bundles, into those epics' archive directories and leave permanent navigation.

## Background

JIT archival never moves files outside `dev/`, so the decks move by explicit relocation. The shared figures directory splits by owner, relative links climbing into `dev/` change depth, and some deck links were already unresolved before the move. Details in `dev/active/fa787f85-documentation-overhaul/investigation.md` §3.4.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each deck bundle (talk, base stylesheet, themes and owned figures) lives under its owning epic's archive directory, and `docs/presentations/` does not exist.
- [hard] REQ-02: Deck prose and claims are unchanged; only link targets change, and every link in each moved bundle resolves, including links that were unresolved before the move.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each owning epic's document references name the new paths and their recorded asset bundles resolve.
- [hard] REQ-04: No permanent page links to a deck, and inbound `dev/active/` citations are repointed.
- [hard] REQ-05: The manifest records each row as complete.
- [hard] REQ-06: The example `crates/gf2-coding/examples/gen_presentation_figures.rs` writes only to an output directory the caller supplies, defaulting to a path under `target/`, and running it writes nothing under `docs/`.
- [hard] REQ-07: The example's header states its purpose and output location in one short paragraph.
- [hard] REQ-08: The Rust CI gate passes.

## Decisions

- DEC-01: The owner decided on 2026-10-03 that this issue owns the figure example's output directory, because the example wrote into `docs/presentations/figures/`.
title: Move presentation decks into their epics' archive dirs
